source.title: International first aid, resuscitation and education guidelines 2020
source.publisher: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)
source.terms: The IFRC allows copies of all or part of the guidelines for non-commercial use, providing the source is acknowledged.

meta.scope_note: For teenagers and adults. Babies and young children need different steps: tell the 112 operator the age.
meta.left_out: Medicine doses are left out on purpose (for example aspirin for chest pain). Ask the 112 operator.

guides.chat_now: Call {number} now, or ask someone to call. Shout and tap their shoulders. If they don't respond, look and listen: are they breathing normally? If not, start CPR: open the guide below.
guides.title: Someone collapsed: start here
guides.when: You are not sure what is wrong.

steps.text: Make sure the place is safe for you, for example from traffic, fire or electricity. Go to the person only when it is safe.
Shout their name and tap their shoulders. Do they respond?
Look at their chest and listen. Are they breathing normally? Gasping, noisy or very slow breathing is NOT normal.

notes: If you are not sure whether they are breathing normally, start CPR. That is what the Red Cross guidelines advise.

guides.title: Not responding and not breathing normally
guides.when: No response to voice or touch, and no breathing or only gasping.

steps.text: Call {number} now, or ask someone nearby to call. Put the phone on speaker so your hands are free.
steps.log: Called or asked someone to call {number}

steps.text: Kneel beside them. Put the heel of one hand in the middle of the chest, the other hand on top, fingers locked together.
With straight arms, push hard, straight down, about 5 cm, then let the chest come all the way back up. Push on every beat: 100 to 120 times a minute.
Keep going without stopping until help takes over, or they cough, open their eyes, move on purpose or breathe normally.

do_not: Do not stop to look for a pulse. A pulse check is unreliable and wastes time.
Do not stop compressions to wait for the ambulance.
notes: If a defibrillator (AED) is nearby, ask someone to bring it, switch it on and follow its voice.
If someone else can take over, swap so you don't get too tired, with as little pause as possible.
If you are carrying the person to hospital, keep CPR going on a firm surface.

guides.title: Not responding but breathing normally
guides.when: No response to voice or touch, but normal, regular breathing.

steps.text: Roll them onto their side and gently tilt their head back. This keeps the airway open and stops them choking if they vomit.
steps.log: Put on their side, airway open

steps.text: Call {number}. Someone who does not respond needs help, even if they breathe.
Stay with them and keep checking their breathing. If they stop breathing normally, start CPR.

do_not: If you think they hurt their neck or back, do not roll them. Keep the airway open by tilting the head and lifting the chin.

guides.chat_now: Act now: if they cannot cough or speak, give up to 5 sharp blows between the shoulder blades, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts, and keep repeating. Ask someone to call {number}. The guide below shows each step.
guides.title: Choking
guides.when: Something is stuck in the throat.

steps.text: Can they cough, speak or breathe?
Tell them to keep coughing. Stay with them and watch closely: it can get worse.
Stand behind them, bend them forward, and give up to 5 sharp blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
Still blocked? Stand behind, put a fist between the belly button and the ribs, hold it with your other hand, and pull sharply in and up, up to 5 times.
Still blocked? Call {number} now. Keep repeating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts.

do_not: Do not sweep inside the mouth blindly with your fingers: it can push the object further down. Only take out something you can see.
notes: Babies under one year need different steps. Tell the 112 operator the age.

guides.chat_now: Press hard on the wound with a cloth and keep pressing. Call {number}, or ask someone to call while you press. Help them lie down.
guides.title: Heavy bleeding
guides.when: Blood is flowing fast from a wound.

steps.text: Press hard on the wound. Use a cloth, bandage or plastic between your hand and the blood. If they can, they can press it themselves.
Help them lie down, so they do not faint and fall.
Call {number}, or ask someone to call while you keep pressing.
If blood soaks through, put another cloth on top and press harder. Do not lift the first cloth.
steps.log: Added a second cloth, pressed harder

steps.text: Only if pressing does not stop heavy bleeding from an arm or leg, and you have a tourniquet: put it on above the wound. The time is saved for the doctor.
Keep them lying down and warm, for example covered with clothes or a blanket.

do_not: If an object such as a knife is stuck in the wound, do not pull it out. Press around it.

guides.chat_now: Call {number} now. Help them sit down and rest, and keep them calm. Ask someone to bring a defibrillator (AED) if there is one nearby.
guides.title: Chest pain
guides.when: Pain or pressure in the chest that does not go away.

steps.text: Help them sit down in a comfortable position. If a doctor prescribed them heart medicine for this, help them take it.
steps.log: Sitting down, helped with own medicine if any

steps.text: Call {number} now. Ask someone to bring a defibrillator (AED) if there is one nearby.
Stay with them, keep them calm, and watch their breathing and whether they respond. If they stop responding and are not breathing normally, start CPR.

notes: Women, older people and people with diabetes may have milder or unusual signs. If in doubt, treat it as serious.
Medicine doses are not given here. Ask the 112 operator what to give.

links.label: They stopped responding or breathing normally

guides.chat_now: Call {number} now: these can be signs of a stroke. Note the time the signs started. Keep them comfortable and give nothing to eat or drink.
guides.title: Signs of a stroke
guides.when: Sudden weak face or arm, or strange speech.

steps.text: Ask them to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift down or not move?
Ask them to repeat a simple sentence. Is their speech slurred or strange?
Any of these signs? Call {number} now. Tell them when the signs started, or the last time the person was seen well. If you don't know, say so.
Help them into a comfortable position and support them so they don't fall. Keep talking to them and watch their breathing.

do_not: Do not give them anything to eat or drink: swallowing may not be safe.
notes: Even if the signs go away, they still need a doctor quickly.
Very high or low blood sugar can look similar. Tell the doctor about diabetes.

guides.chat_now: Call {number} now. Help them lie down and keep as still as possible. Do not tie the limb, cut the bite or suck out the venom.
guides.title: Snakebite
guides.when: Bitten by a snake, or you think so.

steps.text: Help them lie down and keep as still as possible. Moving makes the venom spread faster.
Call {number}. They need a hospital that has antivenom.
Take off rings, bangles, watches and tight clothes near the bite before it swells. Move the limb as little as possible.
If help is far away, keep the bitten arm or leg still with a cloth or non-stretchy bandage wrapped around it. Do not wrap it tight.
Do not let them walk on a bitten leg. Carry them, for example two people making a chair with their arms.
Keep watching their breathing and whether they respond. If it is safe, take a photo of the snake from a distance.

do_not: Do not tie a tight band (tourniquet) around the limb.
Do not cut the bite or suck out the venom.
Do not put ice on it or rub it.
Do not try to catch or kill the snake.

links.label: They stopped responding or breathing normally

guides.chat_now: Move hard or sharp things away and put something soft under their head. Do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth. Call {number} if it lasts more than 5 minutes, it is their first seizure, or they are hurt.
guides.title: Seizure (fit)
guides.when: Shaking, stiffening or not responding with twitching.

steps.text: Tap Done now: the seizure start time is saved for the doctor.
Move hard or sharp things away. Do not move them unless they are in danger, for example on a road.
Put something soft under their head. Take off glasses and loosen anything tight around the neck.
Call {number} if: it is their first seizure, it lasts more than 5 minutes, they are hurt, they don't wake up after, it happens again, they are pregnant or diabetic, or you are not sure.
When the shaking stops, tap Done: the stop time is saved.
Now check their breathing. Are they breathing normally?

do_not: Do not put anything in their mouth or between their teeth.
Do not give them food, drink or medicine until they are fully awake.
